entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Skanderbeg, Gjergj Kastrioti, was a pivotal figure in medieval Albanian history, serving as the leader of the League of Lezhë from 1432 to 1468. As a skilled military commander and statesman, he played a crucial role in defending Albania against the Ottoman Empire, which had been expanding its territories in the Balkans since the 14th century. Skanderbeg's resistance movement, which included a mix of Albanian and Byzantine forces, successfully repelled several Ottoman invasions, buying time for Albania to modernize and develop its own identity.

Skanderbeg's leadership and vision also helped to unite the Albanian nobility and peasantry against the Ottoman threat, laying the groundwork for the modern Albanian nation-state. His legacy extends beyond Albania's borders, inspiring movements for independence and self-determination across the region.

Skanderbeg's life and legacy are a testament to the enduring power of resistance and national identity in the face of overwhelming external pressure.
